name: Clouds ASCII v3
prompt:
Use case: style-transfer
Asset type: Revised ASCII cloud illustration, native near-square PORTRAIT 7:8 composition, target 1173x1341 pixels or native equivalent. This should be only slightly taller than wide.
Input images: Image 1 is the edit target clouds-ascii-v2; preserve its idea of uneven cloud peaks and right-positioned cloud banks, but fix its pale softness. Image 2 is the visual style and color reference s1-clouds; its crisp small ASCII texture, luminous cream colors, dense celadon shading and deep sage shadows are the desired rendering language. Re-render Image 1 in the stronger sharper character-based rendering of Image 2 while adapting the canvas to 7:8.
Required result: Several monumental rounded sculptural cumulus cloud banks clustered across the RIGHT TWO THIRDS, with the strongest form and contrast toward the upper right. Distinct rounded cloud tops at different heights create a natural irregular silhouette. Keep the entire top 5 percent as genuinely clean near-white paper. No cloud touches the upper edge. The clouds descend across the right side and taper irregularly near the bottom, leaving a little clear bottom paper. Right-edge crop allowed. Leftmost 15 percent remains mainly clean paper.
ASCII rendering is essential: Build every cloud volume out of clearly recognizable actual monospaced characters @ # % * + = - : . / |, each about 6 to 8 native pixels tall, dark and sharp enough to remain evident when the full picture is displayed around 800px wide. The alphabet and varying density of characters must be visually evident, like a fine color ASCII terminal rendering. Use denser @ # % and strong deep desaturated sage around #52776A to #345F52 for shadows; celadon and sage characters for midtones; luminous warm cream and pale butter characters to sculpt the large sunlit lobes. Color and density changes within crisp characters create continuous dimensional forms. Preserve the appealing luminous sage-to-cream tonal gradations of Image 2.
Clean edge and background: This is an OPAQUE image on flat near-white neutral paper #f7f7f3. Every pixel must be opaque. Replace all transparency from Image 1 with opaque paper. The external contour is formed by discrete sharp characters becoming sparser and lighter sideways toward the left. Surrounding paper is flat and clean right up to those sparse individual marks. Remove the hazy halo and soft alpha envelope from Image 1 entirely. The cloud top is a clearly bounded natural scalloped outline against empty paper; no overlay or white gradient obscures it.
Constraints: Stronger sage shadows, higher local contrast, crisp ASCII and clean paper are mandatory. No transparent background. No alpha halo. No blur, mist, glow, fog, soft-focus effect, airbrush, gradient fading across the top, photographic grain, stipple-dot substitute, engraving, pixel blocks, oversized coarse glyphs, all-over green tint, words, slogans, frame, oval, watermark, or UI. Keep the full composition native, not a zoomed crop.
reference_roles: clouds-ascii-v2.png: edit target, right cloud banks and uneven peaks
s1-clouds.png: requested crisp ASCII rendering, sage shadows, cream color reference

inspection.ascii: Clearly legible small glyph structures are restored, including @-like marks, plus signs, colons, dashes and other ASCII-like shapes, with strong local contrast. Some marks are stylized or imperfectly formed.
inspection.background: Opaque RGB, no alpha. Clean nearly uniform off-white paper. No soft alpha halo.
inspection.composition: Upper cloud peaks occur at varied heights, entire top 5 percent remains clean paper. Lower cloud ends in sparse glyphs with no hard horizontal cutoff. Most contrast at right; small sparse marks enter the leftmost 15 percent low down.
inspection.aspect_ratio: 1075x1464 is about 0.7343, taller than the requested 7:8 (0.875).
inspection.color: Deeper desaturated sage shadows and brighter cream highlights based on s1-clouds.png. This does not preserve the softer cream/sage palette and tonal balance of clouds-hd.png.

status: Do not adopt under latest user correction
late_user_correction: After this generation completed, user explicitly asked why cloud coloring changed and said they liked earlier coloring. Root clarified that clouds-hd.png (r9/r10 displayed artwork) must be the exact palette and tonal-balance reference. This v3 was generated before that correction arrived and is retained as an unused experiment.
